introduction: A practical joke on a drunken tinker opens a comedy in which clothing, names and performances repeatedly determine how people are treated. In Padua, Baptista's rule that his elder daughter must marry first links Katherina's future to the rival courtships surrounding her younger sister Bianca. A wealthy marriage attracts Petruchio, while Lucentio and his servants improvise disguises to gain access to Bianca. Their schemes develop alongside a contest over authority within marriage, where declarations of affection can accompany coercion and obedience becomes a public spectacle.

fullSynopsis.text: A lord finds the drunken tinker Christopher Sly asleep outside an alehouse and orders an elaborate practical joke. Sly wakes in luxury, surrounded by servants who insist that he is a nobleman recovering from years of delusion. A page dressed as a woman plays his obedient wife and evades his invitation to bed. Players arrive to entertain him with the ensuing comedy. Sly briefly comments after its opening scene, but this edition supplies no later resolution of his story.

In Padua, Baptista will not marry his younger daughter Bianca before her outspoken elder sister Katherina. Bianca's rivals Gremio and Hortensio therefore need a husband for Katherina. Lucentio, newly arrived to study, falls for Bianca and exchanges clothes and identities with his servant Tranio so that he can enter her house as the tutor Cambio. Hortensio also disguises himself as a music teacher, Licio. His friend Petruchio arrives seeking a wealthy wife and readily accepts the challenge of marrying Katherina, undeterred by the accounts of her temper. Tranio, acting as Lucentio, joins the public competition for Bianca.

Katherina's anger at Bianca exposes her resentment of their father's preference. Petruchio negotiates a substantial dowry with Baptista and meets Katherina's insults with extravagant praise and verbal combat. Despite her resistance, he declares that they have agreed to marry on Sunday and explains her public hostility as a private arrangement. Baptista accepts the match. Tranio then outbids Gremio for Bianca with promises of Vincentio's wealth. Baptista requires the father's guarantee, so Tranio must produce a counterfeit Vincentio. Meanwhile Lucentio reveals himself to Bianca through a Latin lesson, and she rejects Hortensio's rival musical courtship.

On the wedding day Petruchio arrives late in absurd clothing. Gremio reports his disruptive conduct during the ceremony, and afterwards he insists on taking Katherina away before the feast, declaring her his property and pretending to protect her from interference. At his country house he abuses the servants, rejects the meal and prevents her rest, presenting deprivation as solicitude for her health. He explicitly describes his purpose as taming her like a hawk. Katherina protests hunger and sleeplessness, but he continues to control food, clothing and travel, even requiring her to accept his account of the time.

Seeing Bianca with Cambio, Hortensio abandons her and turns to a wealthy widow. Tranio recruits a travelling pedant to impersonate Vincentio by falsely warning that Mantuan visitors face death in Padua. The impostor gives Baptista the required financial assurance. While their elders attend to this counterfeit agreement, Biondello helps the real Lucentio and Bianca arrange a secret wedding. On the road back to Padua, Katherina agrees to Petruchio's changing descriptions of the sun and moon and joins his greeting of an old man as a young woman. The traveller proves to be the real Vincentio, whom they escort to his son's lodging.

Vincentio encounters his impersonator, is denied recognition by Biondello and Tranio, and nearly goes to prison as a supposed impostor. Lucentio and Bianca return married and explain the deceptions. Lucentio takes responsibility for his servant's actions, and Vincentio promises to satisfy Baptista, though both fathers remain angry at the trickery. The gathering nevertheless proceeds to a celebratory meal. Petruchio and Katherina, who have watched the exposure, exchange a kiss in the street after he again threatens to take her home if she refuses.

At the feast, Petruchio, Lucentio and Hortensio wager on their wives' obedience. Bianca and the widow refuse their summons, but Katherina comes, fetches the other women and discards her cap at Petruchio's command. Baptista rewards what he considers a transformation with an additional dowry. Katherina delivers a long speech presenting obedience as a wife's debt to her husband's protection and offers to place her hand beneath Petruchio's foot. He celebrates his victory and takes her away to bed. The other husbands express astonishment. Her public conduct secures his triumph, while the play gives no private explanation of her final change.

acts.label: ACT I
acts.summary: Lucentio arrives in Padua to study but immediately falls in love with Bianca. Her father Baptista bars her marriage until Katherina, her elder sister, has a husband. Gremio and Hortensio agree to help remove that obstacle. Lucentio changes identities with Tranio and plans to enter as a tutor; Tranio will maintain the position of a wealthy gentleman and suitor. Sly briefly interrupts the performance from above. Petruchio arrives at Hortensio's house seeking fortune through marriage and agrees to woo Katherina for her wealth. Hortensio arranges to disguise himself as a music teacher, while Gremio unknowingly sponsors Lucentio as another tutor. The competing suitors welcome Petruchio's undertaking.

acts.label: ACT II
acts.summary: Katherina has bound Bianca and demands to know which suitor she prefers. Baptista intervenes, prompting Katherina's complaint that he favours her sister. The suitors present their disguised teachers, and Tranio introduces himself as Vincentio's son Lucentio. Petruchio bargains with Baptista over Katherina's dowry, then hears that she has broken a lute over Hortensio's head. In their private encounter, Petruchio turns her hostility into supposed gentleness and announces his determination to marry her. He tells Baptista that Sunday is agreed and explains away her objections; Baptista approves. Tranio outbids Gremio for Bianca, but the promised marriage depends upon Vincentio guaranteeing the extravagant settlement. Tranio decides to procure a false father.

acts.label: ACT III
acts.summary: Lucentio uses a Latin lesson to reveal his identity and intentions to Bianca. She responds cautiously but leaves room for hope, then rejects Hortensio's musical declaration. Hortensio suspects the rival tutor and threatens to change his choice. Katherina's wedding day begins with Petruchio absent, leaving her humiliated and weeping. He eventually arrives in shabby, mismatched clothing and refuses to change. Gremio later reports his swearing, violence towards the priest and extravagant behaviour during the ceremony. Petruchio then refuses the wedding dinner and, over Katherina's objection, removes her from the company. Meanwhile Tranio continues planning a counterfeit Vincentio, while Lucentio considers stealing a marriage before his rivals can interfere.

acts.label: ACT IV
acts.summary: At Petruchio's house, Katherina finds herself deprived of food and sleep under the claim of loving care. Petruchio explains his method through the training of a hungry hawk and later rejects the new clothes she likes. Hortensio sees Bianca's affection for Cambio, abandons his suit and chooses a widow. Tranio tricks a Mantuan pedant into posing as Vincentio, and the impostor secures Baptista's consent through a financial guarantee. Biondello directs Lucentio towards a private wedding with Bianca. On their journey to Padua, Katherina accepts Petruchio's arbitrary changes between sun and moon and joins his misidentification of Vincentio as a young woman. They learn who he is and accompany him onwards.

acts.label: ACT V
acts.summary: The real Vincentio reaches Lucentio's lodging while his counterfeit occupies the house. Biondello and Tranio deny recognizing him, and Baptista supports having him arrested. Lucentio and Bianca return from their secret wedding, acknowledge their fathers and expose the disguises; the servants and pedant flee. Lucentio assumes responsibility, and Vincentio undertakes to satisfy Baptista. At the ensuing feast, the three husbands bet on whose wife will answer a summons. Only Katherina comes, then brings Bianca and the widow and obeys Petruchio's command to discard her cap. She argues for wives' submission in an extended speech. Petruchio claims victory and leaves with her, as the others marvel at her conduct.

framing.label: Induction
framing.summary: After Christopher Sly quarrels with an alehouse hostess and falls asleep drunk, a hunting lord has him carried into a luxurious room. The lord and servants insist that Sly is a nobleman whose life as a tinker was a prolonged delusion. A page dressed as his wife performs obedience but postpones going to bed with him. Sly accepts his supposed rank and sits with the page to watch the players' comedy. He briefly comments after its first scene; this text does not return to complete the practical joke.
